//attribution: The watcher already reports every change on disk, so the tree stays correct
without this block. What the hook adds is WHO: the agent id that puts a
figure and a beam on the change. Without it every event arrives with an
empty agent, and an empty agent never creates an actor -- the tree updates
Reads (R, violet) are hook-only by nature: the watcher cannot see a file
being opened -- atime is unreliable under relatime and it does not subscribe
to access events -- so without this block there is no read glow at all.
Claude Code reads settings.json at session start, so a session already open
when this file appears keeps running without it. Restart to pick it up.
//lifecycle: Notification, Stop and SubagentStop are not tool calls: they put an agent's
LIFE CYCLE on camera, as distinct from its file operations. A Notification
fires when Claude Code needs permission or has gone idle, and today a
blocked agent looks exactly like a thinking one -- one motionless figure.
Stop and SubagentStop are the facts that let an actor LEAVE; without them
there is only an inference from silence. They carry no matcher, because
they name no tool to match on.
The cost is one more Python process (about 40 ms, measured on this host) on
the agent's loop per firing. These three are cheap because their firing rate
is bounded by HUMAN actions -- a prompt, a turn, a subagent -- rather than
by tool calls, which run in the thousands. That is why these three are
installed and a matcher whose rate scales with the agent's work is a
The session-start caveat above applies to these entries too: a session
already open keeps running without them.
//debugging: RHIZOME_SOCKET overrides the ingest socket and must match the daemon.
RHIZOME_DEBUG_LOG names a file to append hook FAILURES to -- the only
way to tell 'daemon down' from 'nothing happened'.
RHIZOME_TRACE_LOG names a file to append every raw payload to, which is
how you find out what a given Claude Code version puts in the hook JSON.
Prefix either on the command below to enable it.
